items.front: Parallel lines cut by a transversal — which pairs are equal vs supplementary?
items.back: Corresponding, alternate interior and alternate exterior angles are EQUAL; co-interior (same-side interior) angles are SUPPLEMENTARY (180°).

items.front: Triangle angle sum, exterior angle and the inequality?
items.back: Interior angles = 180°; exterior angle = sum of two remote interiors; each side lies strictly between the difference and sum of the other two.

items.front: Pythagorean triples to memorise; similar-triangle area ratio?
items.back: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25 (and multiples). Similar triangles: area ratio = (side ratio)² = k².

items.front: Triangle centres — centroid, circumcentre, incentre, orthocentre?
items.back: Centroid: medians, 2:1 from vertex. Circumcentre: perpendicular bisectors (right triangle: hypotenuse midpoint). Incentre: angle bisectors. Orthocentre: altitudes (right triangle: right-angle vertex).
Bisector from A meets BC at D with BD:DC = AB:AC.

items.front: Circle angle theorems (centre, semicircle, same segment, cyclic quad)?
items.back: Central angle = 2× inscribed on same arc; angle in a semicircle = 90°; angles in the same segment equal; cyclic quad opposite angles sum 180°.
items.examPoint: Circle — central vs inscribed; cyclic quad

items.front: Tangent facts: length, two-tangent angle, tangential quadrilateral?
items.back: Tangent ⟂ radius; length from point at distance d = √(d²−r²); two tangents from a point are equal, with ∠P + central angle = 180°; tangential quad: AB+CD=BC+AD.
Interior sum = (n−2)×180°; exterior sum = 360° (always). Regular: each interior = (n−2)180/n, each exterior = 360/n.

items.front: Coordinate geometry — distance, section, slope, triangle area?
items.back: d=√(Δx²+Δy²); section (m:n) = ((mx₂+nx₁)/(m+n),…); slope=Δy/Δx (perpendicular lines: m₁m₂=−1); area=½|x₁(y₂−y₃)+…|, and zero area means collinear.
items.examPoint: Coordinate geometry — distance, section, slope, area

items.front: Counting integer-sided triangles for perimeter P?
items.back: List a ≤ b ≤ c with a+b+c=P and a+b>c (so c < P/2). Perimeter 14 gives 4 triangles; perimeter 11 gives 4.
